Container.Name: OctoFarm-Redux
Container.Overview:
OctoFarm-Redux is a maintained fork of OctoFarm, whose development stopped at the end of 2022. It unifies multiple OctoPrint instances into one web interface: live status and cameras for every printer, file and filament management, print history and statistics, and bulk commands across the farm.
The application works the same way day to day. This fork brings it to current dependencies, fixes the faults that had accumulated, and adds new features - a rebuilt file manager, camera streaming through the server instead of every browser tab, printer light and maintenance-mode controls, a reworked spool manager, and cancelling a single object mid-print. The image is self-contained - MongoDB runs inside the container - so there is nothing to deploy alongside it.
The session key can be left empty. The container generates one on first start and keeps it in the data volume, so logins survive a restart. Set SUPER_SECRET_KEY yourself only if you would rather manage the key, or need the same key on two installs.
Both MongoDB paths have to be mapped. The mongo base image declares /data/db and /data/configdb as volumes, so leaving /data/configdb unmapped strands an anonymous volume on every redeploy.
Open the web interface after the first start and register the first account; it becomes the administrator.
Container.DonateText: OctoFarm-Redux is free. If it is useful to you, you can leave a tip.

Config.Name: WebUI port
Config.Description: Host port for the web interface. The container always listens on 4000 - the health check checks that port, so do not change OCTOFARM_PORT.

Config.Name: Database
Config.Description: MongoDB data directory. Everything you configure in OctoFarm-Redux lives here: printers, users, history, filament.

Config.Name: Database config
Config.Description: Second volume declared by the mongo base image. It stays empty for a standalone server, but leaving it unmapped strands an anonymous volume on every redeploy.

Config.Name: Thumbnails
Config.Description: Thumbnail store for print history. Same path as upstream OctoFarm, so an existing images folder can be reused.

Config.Name: Logs
Config.Description: Application and process-manager logs. Map it to keep logs across container recreation - the Logs page in the interface reads them from here.

Config.Name: Scripts
Config.Description: Scripts the alert system can run on printer events. Same path as upstream OctoFarm. Leave it mapped even if you use no scripts.

Config.Name: MongoDB log
Config.Description: Where the bundled mongod writes its own log. Only needed if you want to read it from outside the container.

Config.Name: Session key
Config.Description: Signing key for login sessions. Leave empty and the container generates one on first start and keeps it in the data volume, so logins survive a restart. Fill it in only to manage the key yourself - a long random string, 40 or more characters.

Config.Name: Time zone
Config.Description: Container time zone, for example Europe/London. Leave empty for UTC. Timestamps in the history and log views follow it.

Config.Name: Site title
Config.Description: Name shown in the browser tab and the navigation bar.

Config.Name: Log level
Config.Description: One of info, debug or silly. Raise it only while chasing a problem - debug and silly are noisy.

Config.Name: MongoDB connection
Config.Description: Leave this alone unless you want the application to use a MongoDB server elsewhere. The bundled mongod starts either way and listens on 127.0.0.1 inside the container.
